mainEntity.name: Are online lessons suitable for complete beginners?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. There’s no group to keep up with and nothing to feel self-conscious about — we start exactly where you are, whether that’s understanding your camera or finding your way around Lightroom for the first time.
No. Bring whatever you have — a DSLR, mirrorless, bridge or even a phone. The lessons are built around your kit and what you want to achieve with it.

mainEntity.name: Can you help with Lightroom editing over Zoom?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — this is one of the most common reasons people book. Over screen-share we can sort out your folders, imports, duplicates and file naming, then build a repeatable editing workflow on your own images.

mainEntity.name: How much do online photography lessons cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard weekday sessions (9am–5pm Mon–Fri) start at £50 for a single hour, with bundles of 4, 6, 8 or 12 saving up to 25%. If you need evenings or weekends, premium sessions (9am–9pm any day) start at £75 an hour, with the same bundle discounts. You can pay as you go for a single session, or buy a bundle and book the dates later.

mainEntity.name: Can I have lessons in the evening or at weekends?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. As well as standard weekday lessons (9am–5pm Mon–Fri), there’s a premium option that runs 9am–9pm any day, including evenings and weekends. Premium sessions are £75 an hour, with the same bundle discounts of up to 25%. Choose the premium package in the booking box if those times suit you better.

mainEntity.name: How do I book and schedule my Zoom sessions?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a single session, book directly in the online diary and pay at the point of booking. For a bundle, buy the package first — Alan then emails you a diary link and a code that bypasses payment, so you book your dates whenever they suit you. Standard sessions are 9am–5pm Mon–Fri; premium sessions are 9am–9pm any day.

mainEntity.name: What software or setup do I need?

acceptedAnswer.text: A stable internet connection, a laptop, desktop or tablet, and Zoom (free). Alan will share a Dropbox folder so you can send images for review. If you can join a Zoom call and share your screen, you’re ready.

mainEntity.name: How does feedback work between sessions?

acceptedAnswer.text: You’ll leave each session knowing exactly what to practise and why. Many clients also receive a written summary of what was covered, and you can share new images via Dropbox for review in your next session.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer RPS mentoring online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. If you’re working towards an LRPS, ARPS or FRPS distinction, we can run structured panel preparation over Zoom — sequencing, consistency and feedback cycles. RPS clients have a 100% pass rate. See the RPS mentoring page for details.

mainEntity.name: Where can I read reviews from students?

acceptedAnswer.text: You’ll find verified 4 and 5-star reviews across Google and Trustpilot — over 800 in total. There’s a link to them throughout this page.
